intro: The study asked how fresh-session agents use a strategy note when an opponent is instructed to change styles. A tournament win and an average benefit from the note are separate questions.

takeaways.title: FI-005 won the final by 5 HP
takeaways.body: K049 ended 372–367 when time expired. Administrative forfeits do not count as completed bouts.

takeaways.title: No clear benefit from the strategy note
takeaways.body: The note-by-style-change interaction was estimated at +2.44 HP across 50 pairs. The exploratory 95% bootstrap interval of −7.26 to +10.92 HP includes zero.

takeaways.title: Passing on a note is not proof of memory
takeaways.body: Keeping a profile ID and supplying its note to a fresh session does not restore the previous session’s internal memory.

takeaways.title: Replaying the inputs verifies the engine, not the agents
takeaways.body: Running the original commands again reproduced all 94 completed bouts, matching 1,034 native state hashes and 1,128 frame/HP checks. The agents did not decide again.

sections.title: 01 · How to read the archive
body: Fifty qualifying decisions plus forty-nine knockout-bracket decisions make 99 official decisions. Five side-swapped tie-break bouts bring the archive to 104 FightingICE records: 94 completed bouts and 10 forfeits with no final score.
The 100 calibration pairs used fixed bots across four games from 100 Games. They were not live model-agent matches and are separate from FightingICE.
bullets: “Knockout bracket” describes single elimination, not how a bout ended. All 94 completed bouts reached frame 420.
The HP chart uses saved checkpoints. The separate browser replay shows frames from a verified rerun with original artwork, not FightingICE footage.
A bot’s move or hit count may not decide the winner by itself. Game-specific completion, ships sunk, or tie-break rules can also apply.

sections.title: 02 · What the agents saw
body: The 100 fresh profiles all used GPT-6.2 Sol at low reasoning effort. Both seats played ZEN with 400 starting HP in DareFightingICE 7.0.

Both sides committed their commands before the engine advanced each half. At the frame-232 break, they received their opponent’s real message and match state, then submitted a reply and a new command set. The 50 qualifiers produced 100 replies linked to the actual messages sent.

sections.title: 03 · What the experiment found
body: The outcome was the change in HP margin between the break and the end. The interaction estimate was (note/pivot − note/stay) − (neutral/pivot − neutral/stay), grouped by original assignment, including one pair whose assigned note was not delivered.

The interval was wide and did not account for links between some notes with shared origins. Restricting the data to pairs that received their assigned note changes the estimate to +0.98 HP. That is a sensitivity check, not the primary result.
bullets: Note × pivot: +0.54 HP (13 pairs). Note × stay: +0.08 HP (12 pairs).
Neutral × pivot: −0.83 HP (12 pairs). Neutral × stay: +1.15 HP (13 pairs).
Use the 50-pair CSV and Python script below to reproduce the estimates.

sections.title: 04 · Session continuity and limitations
body: Of 98 player seats in the main knockout bracket, 3 continued a verified existing session and 95 started a fresh session under the same profile. The assignment was not randomized, so it cannot tell us which approach performs better.
Twenty-three of 25 opponents assigned to change styles moved their requested commands in the intended direction. Requested commands do not always become executed moves.
bullets: Randomize session continuity and access to a strategy note as separate factors in the next study.
Add opponents and characters, and define the measure of adaptation before collecting data.
